correctness.rationale: The exact published generating function is reproduced with the same Catalan composition. P and G are analytic past radius 1/2 by strict nonnegative-coefficient bounds, and F has only the two dominant boundary singularities. Local expansions give P_+/sqrt(2) times (1-2z)^(-1/2) and -3sqrt(2)P_-/4 times (1+2z)^(1/2). Coefficient transfer gives a_n=K 2^n n^-1/2(1+(alpha+beta(-1)^n)/n+O(n^-2)) with beta=3P_-/(4P_+)>0. Direct subtraction proves the stated nonzero signed Turán constant; independent finite enumeration and exact-series checks corroborate, without replacing, the asymptotic proof.

value.rationale: This determines an infinite qualitative shape phenomenon that first-order growth does not resolve: strict log-concavity and strict log-convexity alternate by parity for all sufficiently large indices. The exact nonzero leading Turán constant explains how a subleading negative singularity dominates adjacent-curvature despite the positive singularity governing counts. It rules out both eventual one-sided coefficient-shape properties and gives a concrete test case in permutation-pattern enumeration; no arbitrary finite slice or routine coefficient table is presented.
